item.title: Beneath Ceaseless Skies - 2026 Awards-Eligible Stories from &lt;i&gt;BCS&lt;/i&gt; by Scott H. Andrews
item.description: For readers interested in nominating for awards, such as the Hugos or Nebulas, in 2026, here are the eligible stories from BCS in 2025 and which awards category they fit in. Thank you for your interest in our stories! What BCS Stories are Eligible: Everything published in 2025, which is BCS #423 through BCS #447. item.title: Beneath Ceaseless Skies - Slush Update, 12/21/25 by Scott H. Andrews
item.description: All submissions to Beneath Ceaseless Skies sent on or before November 24, 2025 have now been replied to. If you sent a submission on or before Nov. 24 and you have not received a response, please first check your spam filter (especially if your email address is a gmail.com, hotmail.com, or any yahoo address), then query us using the email form on our Contact Page or send an email to “query” at the magazine’s domain name. Include the story’s title and the email address from which you submitted it

item.title: Beneath Ceaseless Skies - <i>BCS</i> Stories on <i>Locus</i> 2025 Recommended Reading List by Scott H. Andrews
item.description: Four novelettes from BCS made the 2025 Recommended Reading List from Locus magazine, the top review source in the field, as compiled by their insightful team of short fiction reviewers and outside editors. The BCS pieces named to the list: Novelette: “Our Echoes Drifting Through the Marsh,” Marie Croke (BCS #423, 01/09/25) “Last Train from Deadwall,” André Geleynse (BCS #433, 05/29/25) “The City of Tears,” Molly Tanzer (BCS #429, 04/03/25) “A Random Walk Through the Goblin Library,” Chris Willri

item.title: Beneath Ceaseless Skies - “Our Echoes Drifting Through the Marsh” by Marie Croke a Finalist for the Nebula Awards by Scott H. Andrews
item.description: “Our Echoes Drifting Through the Marsh” by Marie Croke, from BCS #423, has been named a finalist for the 2025 Nebula Awards, Best Novelette. Congratulations! “Our Echoes Drifting Through the Marsh” is a great story of love pit against barriers of society, identity, and fate. You can read it here, if you haven’t already.
